info.title: Aivi API
info.description: Update Aivi Live Activities and widgets on your iPhone with a single HTTP request. Guides and examples: https://docs.getaivi.app/api-reference/

400.description: `Template mismatch`: `content.template` is not the template the resource was created with.

401.description: `Could not validate credentials`: the `Authorization` header is missing, malformed, or the token is unknown.

402.description: `No active subscription was found`: the token is valid but the account has no active subscription. `code` is `subscription_inactive`, and `expired_at` says when the last subscription ended, or is `null` if there never was one.

404.description: `Activity not found`: no activity with that `slug` exists on your account.

422.description: `Too many ongoing activities`: starting this activity would exceed the concurrent-activity quota. Or an array of field errors: the body failed validation, or the content (with the activity's name) makes a Live Activity push larger than Apple's 4096-byte limit (`type` `payload_too_large`, at `content`).

put.description:
Replaces the widget's webhooks with the given map and returns it, redacted. Aivi calls a webhook for each press on the widget, with the event envelope as the default body. Keys don't have to match the actions the widget shows right now, so you can configure webhooks before you publish the actions. A validation error never echoes a secret, a header value, or a query value.

Redacted means the `secret` is never returned, and header values and the values in the URL's query string come back as `"***"`.

Guide: https://docs.getaivi.app/events/#webhooks

get.description:

Redacted means the `secret` is never returned, and header values and the values in the URL's query string come back as `"***"`.

get.description:
Opens a server-sent event stream of your account's events: `widget.action.v1` for presses on a widget's actions, such as a switchboard's tiles (subject `widget/<slug>`), and `activity.action.v1` for presses on a Live Activity's actions, such as a remote's buttons (subject `activity/<slug>`). One stream carries the events of every widget and Live Activity on your account; filter it with `types` and `subject`.

Each event arrives as an `id:` line with the stream's position, then a `data:` line holding the event envelope as JSON. The stream opens with a `retry:` line and its starting position, and a `: ping` comment arrives every 20 seconds while nothing else happens.

The server closes every stream after 15 minutes: reconnect after the `retry:` delay, and send the last `id:` you saw as `Last-Event-ID` to replay the events you missed that haven't expired yet. An event can arrive twice, so deduplicate on its `id`. At most 4 streams per account.

When a stream can't be set up for now, for example while the database is unavailable, the answer is still `200`: a stream that holds only a `retry:` line and ends. Reconnect after the delay.

Guide: https://docs.getaivi.app/events/

parameters.name: types

schema.description: Only events of these types, for example `widget.action.v1` or `activity.action.v1`. Repeatable. Omit for every type.
schema.title: Types

parameters.description: Only events of these types, for example `widget.action.v1` or `activity.action.v1`. Repeatable. Omit for every type.

parameters.name: subject

schema.description: Only events about these resources, written as `<kind>/<slug>`, for example `widget/living-room` or `activity/vacuum`. Repeatable. Omit for every subject.
schema.title: Subject

parameters.description: Only events about these resources, written as `<kind>/<slug>`, for example `widget/living-room` or `activity/vacuum`. Repeatable. Omit for every subject.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

schema.description: The last `id:` this client received, exactly as sent. The stream first replays the unexpired events after it. Without it nothing is replayed.
schema.title: Last-Event-Id

parameters.description: The last `id:` this client received, exactly as sent. The stream first replays the unexpired events after it. Without it nothing is replayed.

schema.description:
Server-sent events (`text/event-stream`), UTF-8, one event per block, blocks separated by a blank line:

- `retry: <ms>`: first, the reconnect delay.
- `id: <cursor>` alone: the stream's starting position.
- `: ping`: a comment every 20 seconds while nothing else happens. Ignore it.
- `id: <cursor>` then `data: <json>`: one event. `data` is a single line holding one JSON event envelope; `x-sse-data-schema` names its schema (`WidgetActionEvent` for `widget.action.v1`, `ActivityActionEvent` for `activity.action.v1`). Send the last `id` back as `Last-Event-ID` when you reconnect.

text/event-stream.example:
retry: 1000
id: u:6

: ping

id: u:7
data: {"id":"7c1e5b0a-4d2f-5a8e-9b3c-2f6d8e1a4c57","request_id":"act_3f9c2a71b04e","type":"widget.action.v1","subject":{"kind":"widget","slug":"living-room"},"occurred_at":"2026-10-01T19:04:07.512000Z","expires_at":"2026-10-01T19:04:12.512000Z","data":{"action":"porch","kind":"toggle","value":true}}

id: u:8
data: {"id":"0d9a7f3e-6b21-5c48-8e1f-4a7c3b2d9e60","request_id":"act_8b2e61d4c90a","type":"activity.action.v1","subject":{"kind":"activity","slug":"vacuum"},"occurred_at":"2026-10-01T19:05:41.207000Z","expires_at":"2026-10-01T19:05:46.207000Z","data":{"action":"pause","kind":"button","instance_id":"0b6f1c8e-2d4a-4e57-9a3b-6c1d2e3f4a5b"}}

Stat-Input.title: Stat
Stat-Input.description:
One labelled reading, e.g. Range 312 km. `unit` is drawn smaller
after the value; `""` draws none.

`icon` is a symbol name that stands in for the label where the stat
is shown alone, on the Lock Screen (circular, inline and the
rectangular lead); the widget's `icon` is used when it is absent.
Home Screen rows stay text only. A name only, not an `Icon`: the
value's `text_color` tints it.

`max` makes the stat a gauge filled `value / max`. It needs a plain
number in `value.value` (e.g. `78` or `-3.5`) and no formatter. A
reading past either end is taken as sent and the device clamps the
fill to 0 to 1, since live readings overshoot. Without `max`, the
device still draws a gauge for a 0 to 100 value with a `%` unit.

Stat-Output.title: Stat
Stat-Output.description:
One labelled reading, e.g. Range 312 km. `unit` is drawn smaller
after the value; `""` draws none.

`icon` is a symbol name that stands in for the label where the stat
is shown alone, on the Lock Screen (circular, inline and the
rectangular lead); the widget's `icon` is used when it is absent.
Home Screen rows stay text only. A name only, not an `Icon`: the
value's `text_color` tints it.

`max` makes the stat a gauge filled `value / max`. It needs a plain
number in `value.value` (e.g. `78` or `-3.5`) and no formatter. A
reading past either end is taken as sent and the device clamps the
fill to 0 to 1, since live readings overshoot. Without `max`, the
device still draws a gauge for a 0 to 100 value with a `%` unit.

SubscriptionInactiveDetail.title: SubscriptionInactiveDetail
SubscriptionInactiveDetail.description:
A `402`: the token is valid, but the account has no active
subscription. `detail` stays human-readable; `code` and `expired_at`
are for clients that act on it.

SwitchboardWidgetContent-Input.title: SwitchboardWidgetContent
SwitchboardWidgetContent-Input.description:
A grid of action tiles: buttons and toggles the user presses on the
Home Screen. Eight is the cap: it fills the large widget's grid, and
eight plain actions serialize to about 1 KB against the 4 KiB content
limit. Marks (subtitle, gradient, image) and custom state words
(`state_text`) cost more; eight fully dressed actions can pass it,
and the content limit rejects those rather than a tighter per-field
cap (see `Image`).

SwitchboardWidgetContent-Output.title: SwitchboardWidgetContent
SwitchboardWidgetContent-Output.description:
A grid of action tiles: buttons and toggles the user presses on the
Home Screen. Eight is the cap: it fills the large widget's grid, and
eight plain actions serialize to about 1 KB against the 4 KiB content
limit. Marks (subtitle, gradient, image) and custom state words
(`state_text`) cost more; eight fully dressed actions can pass it,
and the content limit rejects those rather than a tighter per-field
cap (see `Image`).

ToggleAction-Input.title: ToggleAction
ToggleAction-Input.description:
A two-state action. `on` is publisher-owned: a press posts the
requested value and the publisher confirms it with new content. The
label and the glyph are the same in both states, as in Control
Center: the tile's fill is what says on or off.

ToggleStateText.title: ToggleStateText
ToggleStateText.description:
A toggle's words for its states, each replacing the app's own
(in parentheses). A missing key or `null` keeps the app's word, `""`
shows none, and every key stands alone: renaming `on` leaves
`turning_on` as it was. VoiceOver still announces the app's word for
a state whose word is hidden.

TrendWidgetContent-Input.title: TrendWidgetContent
TrendWidgetContent-Input.description:
A current reading with a compact history sparkline.

`points` is the recent history, oldest first; the device scales it to
the sparkline. The cap keeps the densest payload well under the 4 KiB
content limit.

url.title: Url
url.description: The URL to call. Must start with `https://`. May contain placeholders such as `{{action}}`.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Extra request headers, up to 1 KiB in total. `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Connection`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Proxy-Authorization`, and any name starting with `X-Aivi-` are refused.

body.description: A JSON template of up to 2 KiB whose strings may contain placeholders. Omit it, or send `null`, to receive the event envelope as the body.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Turns on request signing: each request then carries `X-Aivi-Timestamp` and an HMAC-SHA256 `X-Aivi-Signature`. Use a long random string. Never returned.

WebhookConfig.title: WebhookConfig
WebhookConfig.description:
A request template: Aivi fills it in for each event and sends it
to `url`. Every request carries `Idempotency-Key: <event id>`, and
every request except a `GET` carries `Content-Type: application/json`.

WidgetData-Input.title: WidgetData
WidgetData-Input.description:
Request and response body, mirroring the activity endpoint's shape.

The response reports the stored state rather than echoing the request:
`stale_after` is the widget's effective setting, which the request may
have left untouched by omitting the field.
